product.schneider-eurosx16.summary: The 16 MHz configuration of the EuroSX desktop.
product.schneider-eurosx16.history: In May 1991, Micromineiro advertised a 16 MHz EuroSX in Portugal for 260,000 escudos, plus monitor and VAT. The offer positioned the 386SX as an entry point to 32-bit computing. In May 1992, IFS advertised the /16–40 configuration.
product.schneider-eurosx16.technical.con: The disk differs across the commercial documentation. The manual lists 40 MB, the 1991 ad specifies 42 MB for its 16 MHz EuroSX, and the 1992 ad uses the designation /16–40.
product.schneider-eurosx16.technical.boa: The board integrates memory logic and video. The manual shows VLSI VL82C331, BIGJIM at U33 and ATI 28800 at U45. It distinguishes the 16 and 20 MHz boards.
product.schneider-eurosx16.technical.fir: The ROM is split across two chips. The manual identifies LOW and HIGH at U9 and U10. A boot photograph of a EuroSX shows system BIOS 1.05 and VGA 3.01a. These versions still need to be matched to a specific configuration and the dumps preserved.
product.schneider-eurosx16.technical.ver: BluMach has a documentary sheet. A dedicated model and boot validation remain pending.
product.schneider-eurosx16.technical.lim: System and video dumps and comparison of the board map are pending. A photograph suitable for publication is still needed.
product.schneider-eurosx16.technical.man: Schneider, Service Manual EURO 386 SX / L 386/16
